Question: Let \(S\) be the square one of whose diagonals has endpoints \((0.1, 0.7)\) and \((-0.1, -0.7).\) A point \(v = (x, y)\) is chosen uniformly at random over all pairs of real numbers \(x\) and \(y\) such that \(0 \le x \le 2012\) and \(0 \le y \le 2012.\) Let \(T(v)\) be a translated copy of \(S\) centered at \(v.\) What is the probability that the square region determined by \(T(v)\) contains exactly two points with integer coordinates in its interior?
